PullRequest.Title: sessions: add remote session delegation tools
PullRequest.Body: Fixes #336682 Adds picker-free remote delegation in the Agents window: - `list_agent_hosts` / `create_remote_session`: resource and model filtering with least-loaded host placement. - `send_remote_message`: exact-chat follow-ups and replies, including background approvals and busy-chat queues. - `get_remote_session`: read-only status and latest-response inspection. Off by default via `chat.remoteSessions.tools.enabled`, with automatic experiment defaults (`config.chat.remoteSessions.tools.enabled`) and explicit user overrides. Applies to tool visibility and invocation; disabling leaves connected hosts and running sessions intact. Supports workspace-less sessions or an existing trusted target folder/worktree. Requires compatible hosts and a connected coordinating window. Cloning and budget redesign remain separate follow-ups. **New setting to enable remote sessions** **Remote Sessions tools in Chat Customizations** **Sample Cross-Host Interaction**

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The added map/Promise.all call path is explicit; `RemoteAgentHostSessionsProvider.mapWorkingDirectoryUri` converts each file URI to that host's `vscode-agent-host` authority, and `AgentHostFileSystemProvider.stat` forwards it through `resourceResolve`. Protocol requests have no request timeout, while `raceCancellationError` only races the caller token and does not cancel the underlying RPC. The only uncertain factor is how many hosts a typical user connects, which affects severity rather than the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: remote filesystem `resourceResolve` RPCs and their pending protocol request objects
Findings.PerformanceScaling: One stat RPC is issued for every eligible connected remote provider (H calls in parallel), and completion latency is the maximum of all H probes; a non-returning probe leaves the creation pending until external cancellation or connection closure.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased latency and blocked critical path
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR there was no remote-session placement path that broadcast a workspace stat across all connected agent hosts; ordinary creation targets one provider/workspace.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Remote creation with a target-local file URI now probes every eligible connected host concurrently and waits for all probes before selecting the least-loaded host.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 202 introduces `Promise.all(this.remoteProviders().map(...))`, and RIGHT line 207 performs `fileService.stat(candidate.workspace)` inside that per-provider map. For an unqualified `file:` workspace, `getCandidate` maps the same path into every eligible remote host, so this diff creates one remote filesystem RPC per host and awaits the whole fan-out before placement.
Findings.Title: Bound cross-host workspace probes during placement
Findings.Impact: Creating a remote session for `file:///...` can hang on one unrelated slow/reconnecting host even when another healthy host is eligible; larger host fleets also receive a burst of simultaneous filesystem RPCs.
Findings.Evidence: `RemoteSessionService.candidates` maps an unqualified workspace to each provider, launches all validations with `Promise.all`, and calls `IFileService.stat` for each. The mapped scheme is backed by `AgentHostFileSystemProvider.stat`, which awaits a remote `resourceResolve` JSON-RPC. `AgentHostProtocolClient._dispatchRequest` registers the pending request without a timeout and deliberately waits through reconnect cycles. Therefore one slow/reconnecting candidate blocks the entire creation request, and H eligible hosts produce H simultaneous remote filesystem calls.
Findings.Recommendation: Bound candidate probing with a shared concurrency limiter and a per-host deadline. Treat a timed-out host as rejected and continue with healthy candidates; preserve exact-host behavior by probing only the pinned host when `hostId` or a host-qualified workspace is supplied.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The full-catalog scan, URI/label retention, and whole-result JSON serialization are direct. `BaseAgentHostSessionsProvider.getSessions` returns every entry in `_sessionCache`; only persisted startup snapshots are capped at 100, while a successful live `listSessions()` repopulates the cache from the full host result. Exact user catalog sizes are uncertain, so severity is low.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cost grows with the effective number of distinct workspace URIs across every connected host after deduplication; the scan additionally grows with total sessions, even when many map to the same workspace.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: CPU/GC pressure and increased tool latency
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR no language-model tool scanned every remote provider's session catalog and serialized its workspace inventory into a prompt-visible result.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new `list_agent_hosts` tool exports all distinct workspaces from each connected host's complete in-memory session catalog into one language-model tool result.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 116 walks every session returned by every remote provider and accumulates every distinct workspace without a limit; `ListAgentHostsTool.invoke` then serializes the resulting structure in full with `JSON.stringify({ hosts })` at RIGHT line 45.
Findings.Title: Cap workspace inventory before serializing host lists
Findings.Impact: Users with long-lived hosts or many repositories can get a very large tool result, increasing list-tool latency, allocation/GC pressure, and model-context consumption before the agent can continue.
Findings.Evidence: `describeHost` deduplicates workspaces but never bounds their effective cardinality, and `listHosts` repeats this for all remote providers. The tool then pretty-prints the entire object, allocating and passing all bytes downstream. On connected hosts, `_refreshSessions` inserts the complete `connection.listSessions()` response into `_sessionCache`, so the live result is not constrained by the 100-entry persistence cap.
Findings.Recommendation: Cap workspaces per host before constructing/serializing the result (prefer the most recently used entries) and include total/truncated metadata so callers can request or target a narrower inventory without materializing the full catalog.

Scenarios.Scenario: List remote agent hosts and known workspaces
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Synchronous scans of all provider sessions/models and full JSON serialization must complete before `list_agent_hosts` returns. Any cold catalog refresh launched by `getSessions()` is asynchronous and is not awaited by this invocation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh a remote host's complete session catalog when its cache has not initialized.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one cold `listSessions` RPC per remote provider because `_ensureSessionCache` coalesces in-flight refreshes; zero on a warm initialized cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Providers could already refresh for existing UI consumers, but the new tool adds another cold caller across every remote provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The refresh is launched but not awaited, so it is off this invocation's critical path; the current cache is scanned immediately.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize the complete host inventory to JSON.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One pretty-printed serialization containing all hosts, agents/models, and every distinct workspace found in their current full session catalogs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No remote-host language-model tool constructed this combined inventory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Directly blocks tool completion and creates the prompt-visible result.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Connected host count, total sessions scanned, and effective distinct workspace URIs after per-host deduplication.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Hosts are processed synchronously by `Array.map`; any cold provider catalog refreshes can run independently across hosts. JSON serialization is one synchronous operation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Provider session catalogs and registered model metadata are reused when warm. A cold `provider.getSessions()` can start one coalesced asynchronous `listSessions()` refresh per provider, but the tool returns the currently available cache. Workspace inventory is deduplicated by URI but not capped or otherwise cached as a bounded projection.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: full session scans, distinct-workspace accumulation, and uncapped JSON serialization are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical distinct-workspace counts are unknown; connected live catalogs are not bounded by the 100-entry persisted startup-cache cap, so long-lived hosts can materially exceed small inventories.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable low-severity serialization/allocation regression because the newly exposed tool materializes an uncapped catalog into model-visible JSON.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create a remote session with automatic host placement
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Resolving the exact source session, validating all candidate hosts, selecting one, creating/configuring its session, acquiring the background chat, and accepting the first prompt all block completion. For an unqualified file workspace, every candidate stat is awaited before selection.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Subscribe to and read originating remote session state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One temporary source-session subscription/read per creation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No remote delegation creation path resolved an originating host session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must provide verified source identity/depth before placement.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Validate that the requested target-local workspace exists and is a directory on each candidate host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: For an unqualified file URI, one remote `resourceResolve`/stat per eligible connected host; a host-qualified workspace or host ID effectively narrows this to one.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Ordinary session creation addressed one provider/workspace and did not broadcast filesystem probes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All probes are awaited; the slowest or non-returning host blocks placement.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create/configure a remote session, load its chat model, and submit the initial prompt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One session creation/send on the selected host and one background chat acquire/load; no per-candidate creation fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This cross-host background creation workflow did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both are required before the tool reports the session started; the retained model is released when idle.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Eligible connected host count H for file-workspace validation; workspace-less creation performs no stat fan-out.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Candidate workspace validation uses unbounded `Promise.all` across eligible providers. After selection only one host creation proceeds. Pending-creation counters influence placement but do not limit aggregate candidate probes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Creation requests are coalesced by source/request ID and retained up to 25 per window. Candidate workspace stats have no positive/negative cache and are repeated for distinct creation calls. Registered model/session state is read from warm in-memory catalogs when available.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: URI mapping reaches the remote filesystem provider, which sends an un-timed `resourceResolve`; outer cancellation races but does not cancel the underlying RPC.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Fleet sizes and remote RPC durations vary, but the absence of a per-probe deadline and protocol request timeout makes the slowest-host dependency real at any fleet size above one.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity boundary fan-out because H remote stat calls are launched together and all must settle before a healthy host can be selected.

Scenarios.Scenario: Send a remote follow-up or reply to the originating chat
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Source resolution, target session/chat snapshots, workspace trust checks, client-tool preparation, dispatch, and host acknowledgement block the send result. The subsequent model turn runs asynchronously after acknowledged queueing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One source-session read plus one target-session and one target-chat subscription per send; source and target may be on different hosts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No cross-host exact-chat send path performed these reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All three state reads validate exact identity/interactivity before dispatch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load/retain the target chat, claim client tools, enqueue one message, and await acknowledgement.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cold chat-model load and client-tool preparation for the target, reused when already warm; one queue dispatch and acknowledgement wait.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing visible-chat flows could load models, but this diff adds background cross-host acquisition and direct queueing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Preparation and acknowledgement must finish before returning `sent`/`queued`; model execution itself is off the result critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Up to 50 admitted sends per window, serialized per exact target chat; multi-root trust checks scale with target folder count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Sends are FIFO-serialized per exact target chat by `SequencerByKey`; different target chats can run concurrently, with the window-wide request cap bounding total admitted sends at 50.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Send requests are coalesced by source/request ID and capped at 50 per window. Protocol subscriptions are temporary/ref-counted. `acquireOrLoadSession` reuses an existing warm model; cold targets load once per active reference. Background model references remain until active and queued requests are both idle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: ordering, caps, temporary subscription disposal, and idle release are explicit and covered by changed tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cold model/history load duration depends on target history and connection latency; the request cap and per-chat sequencer bound retained references and same-chat pressure.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional reportable regression: expensive work is necessary for identity/trust, same-chat sends are sequenced, aggregate admission is capped, and retained models have explicit idle/disconnect cleanup.

Scenarios.Scenario: Inspect a remote session's current status and latest response
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Exact host/provider resolution and verified session/chat snapshots must complete before returning. A 10-second cancellation timeout bounds the operation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read verified remote session and chat protocol state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one session subscription and one exact-chat subscription for the requested target.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No one-shot remote inspection tool existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both reads are required to construct the current snapshot; the 10-second timer bounds waiting.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One bounded JSON serialization whose response/error text is capped at 16 KiB each and only the latest turn is included.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No remote inspection result was serialized.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Serialization completes before the tool result is returned.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One exact target per invocation; response/error projection is capped at 16 KiB.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each invocation performs one independent inspection; no internal fan-out. Call concurrency is controlled by the tool caller rather than a new loop in this implementation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Inspection intentionally does not use cached chat-model content; it reads current verified protocol state. Temporary subscriptions are disposed after each call and unavailable results are not cached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: exact two-subscription flow, timeout, disposal, and output caps are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Protocol snapshot size before projection depends on the host state, but output assembly stops after the bounded latest response and excludes older transcript/tool content.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression: boundary cardinality is constant, waiting is timed out, subscriptions are disposed, and serialized text is bounded.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 59 changed files. Reported one cross-host remote-filesystem fan-out/latency issue and one uncapped host-inventory serialization issue; verified queueing, coalescing, request caps, model-reference cleanup, temporary subscription disposal, and bounded inspection output for the remaining scenarios.
